The execution boundary

Keep model choice separate from authority.

Agents can run on local, enterprise-hosted or frontier models. Light governs identity, authorization, scope, approval, tool access, state, audit, execution and reconciliation before any of them reach your systems.

Why a prompt is not enough

Enforcement has to live outside the model.

An instruction is a request. A permission is a fact. Three things have to be true outside the model for the difference to hold.

  • 01

    Instructions are requests, not limits

    A model can ignore a rule in its prompt, misread it, or be argued out of it. Nothing written in a prompt is a boundary, however firmly it is worded.

  • 02

    Permissions sit outside the model

    Identity, scope and approval are checked by the execution layer. The model can ask for something; it cannot grant itself anything.

  • 03

    Every action leaves evidence

    What was requested, what the policy decided, who approved it and what actually happened are all recorded, so somebody can check afterwards.

Control fields + business context

Flexible data. Unambiguous control.

Information specific to one customer should not mean rebuilding the platform. Combine known control fields with flexible business payloads, evidence, reasoning instructions and structured output.

  • 01

    Controlled structured fields

    Authorization, routing, enforcement, thresholds and state changes use explicit structured data. A sentence inside a business document does not grant permission.

  • 02

    Flexible business payload

    Documents, text and JSON carry the context of the job. Their evidence and instructions stay separate from the control fields the platform trusts.

  • 03

    Validated output

    Check structured output against what the workflow expects, then apply the human or policy boundary before it returns to an existing process.

Model placement

Use the model that fits the work.

Choose on security, capability, performance and cost. The control model stays the same across providers, and no single model is best at everything.

  1. 01

    Local / private models

    An option for sensitive data, within your own data controls and whatever your team can realistically operate.

  2. 02

    Enterprise-hosted AI

    Controlled serving and access for workloads that belong on your enterprise platform.

  3. 03

    Frontier APIs

    An option for genuinely hard reasoning, when your data policy allows an external service.

  4. 04

    Smaller models

    Worth evaluating for classification, extraction and routine processing, where a large model earns nothing.

Start with the systems you already run.

Bring the problem, the data you already have and the outcome you need. You do not need to choose a model or a framework first. Booking a demo prepares an email on your device — you decide whether to send it.
